title: The three digits of a three-digit number
keyIdea: In a three-digit number the digits stand for hundreds, tens and ones — so 347 means 3 hundreds + 4 tens + 7 ones, not 3+4+7 and not a swap of places.
familyTip: Write 347. Ask: how many hundred flats? How many ten rods? How many ones? Build it with base-ten blocks if you have them.

visual.caption: Three-digit place idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: a zero can hold an empty place

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build 241 on H–T–O, expand 347, name hundreds-digit worth, read 305 with zero, catch digit-sum myth, build 516.

kid: A three-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones places.
The left digit tells how many hundreds. The middle tells tens. The right tells ones.
347 means 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones — not 3 plus 4 plus 7.
A zero can hold a place, like the 0 tens in 305.
adult: CCSS 2.NBT.1: understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens and ones; 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens (called a hundred). Distinct from The two digits of a two-digit number, A Hundred Is Ten Tens (bundling), Counting within 1,000 (hops), and The multiples of 100.
Words: hundreds, tens, ones, place value, expand, placeholder zero. Common mistakes: summing digits; swapping places; reading the hundreds digit as tens or ones; ignoring zero as a place holder.
In the lab your child builds 241 on an H–T–O chart, expands 347, names what the hundreds digit is worth, reads 305 with a zero tens place, spots the digit-sum mix-up, and builds 516.

practice.hint: Hundreds are worth 100 each. Do not add the digits as ones.
practice.explain: 2×100 + 4×10 + 1 = 241. Summing to 7 or swapping places is a mix-up.

practice.hint: Left = hundreds, middle = tens, right = ones.
Which place is the 5 sitting in?
practice.explain: The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it means five hundreds.

practice.hint: The left digit of a three-digit number.

pool.hint: Zero can hold the tens place.
Match each digit to its place.
A multiple of 100 still has three places.
Spot the digit-summing mix-up among the choices.
pool.explain: Digits name place values; summing them as ones is the mix-up.

pool.hint: Do not reverse or sum the digits.
Tens sit in the middle place.

pool.prompt: Place value for three digits means…
choices: each digit’s worth depends on hundreds, tens or ones place
pool.hint: Think of the hundreds–tens–ones chart places.
pool.explain: The same digit means hundreds, tens or ones depending on place.

pool.hint: The ones digit is the rightmost digit of the number.
